Owner coverage ruling of 2026-08-30, given over the Step D drafts in verification/reviews/packets/coverage-drafts-2026-08-30.md. D2-B, APPROVED WITH THE ONE SECURITY-CONSEQUENCE CORRECTION THE RULING REQUIRED. The draft said *revealing a receipt discloses nothing*. That does not follow from the receipt carrying digests rather than plaintext, and it is deleted. What the theorem states instead is the narrow fact: the receipt does not itself carry the retained call bytes, and this claim establishes no confidentiality, no unlinkability, and no resistance to inference or to guessing a low-entropy reconstruction and confirming it against the commitment. The same sentence had settled in `scitt/mod.rs`'s module documentation and is corrected there in the same change — one claim written down twice is still one claim, and fixing only the registry copy would relocate it. The truncation consequence the ruling asked to keep is kept and is evidenced: the ChainLabel is inside what the commitment covers, so a truncated call cannot become COMPLETE, and probe M80 establishes that the correspondence check is what makes it so.
